title: pulse-probe coldstart diary
content:
Purpose / motivation:
Quick, personal log for a pulse-probe experiment aimed at isolating cold-start contributions to 95/99/99.9 latency during short microbursts (5–30s). Want to understand how much of the observed tail in prod-like bursts is: (A) model cold KV cache refill, (B) GPU context warmup and CUDA kernel JIT, (C) ingress queuing jitter, or (D) orchestration-level delays (container spin, network attach). This is a scratchpad — incomplete, messy, but captures the configs and raw takeaways before I forget them.

Experiment summary (high level):
- Workload: synthetic small-burst traffic that mimics chat usage: 1–20 concurrent short requests (avg 8 tokens generated), bursts last 5s, 15s, 30s; idle between bursts random 30–300s to force cold conditions.
- Target binary: r-inference serving-runtime main (commit a3f8b2) with small-mod: disable proactive KV prefetch for these runs.
- Model: open-llama-7b variant, FP16, no quantization, sequence length = 128.
- Fleet config: single GPU node (A100 40GB), 1 container, no multi-tenant noise. System under limited isolation to approximate Dedicated single-tenant but not full private network.
- Instrumentation: token-level traces (client-side timestamps), server-side spans (request arrival, scheduling, first-token, end), nvml GPU metrics (power, mem), dmesg for driver jitter.

Key knobs tried / rationale:
- cold gap (idle time before burst): 30s, 120s, 300s — to see decay of hot caches and other ephemeral state.
- prewarm flag: on/off — spawns a dry-run request during idle to keep kernels hot.
- batch window: 5ms, 20ms — to see queuing tradeoffs for 5–20 concurrent arrivals.
- kv-cache retention: 1s, 10s, infinite — test whether KV eviction policy is main tail driver.
- driver warmup (CUDA jit): run initial compile-only pass before bursts in some trials.

Representative raw numbers (median / p95 / p99 in ms) — these are synthetic & noisy but directional:
- Burst 5s, idle 30s, prewarm off, batch=5ms, kv=1s:
  median: 42ms, p95: 180ms, p99: 740ms
- Burst 5s, idle 120s, prewarm off, batch=5ms, kv=1s:
  median: 58ms, p95: 320ms, p99: 1,200ms
- Burst 15s, idle 120s, prewarm on (dry-run every 60s), batch=5ms, kv=10s:
  median: 51ms, p95: 120ms, p99: 300ms
- Burst 30s, idle 300s, prewarm off, batch=20ms, kv=infinite:
  median: 70ms, p95: 400ms, p99: 1,800ms

Immediate observations (raw interpretation):
- Short idle (30s) gives much better tail than long idle (120–300s) — suggests a mixture of ephemeral kernel/jit and KV cache decay.
- Enabling prewarm (a single small compile/request) dramatically lowers p99 in the 120s idle case (1,200ms -> ~300ms). That points strongly to driver/JIT/initial kernel compile and/or memory allocations as a major component.
- Increasing batch window to 20ms reduces median at moderate concurrency but seems to increase p99 in cold conditions (probably because cold requests get batched with background prewarm/other work leading to longer per-request end-to-end).
- kv retention helps for bursts longer than kv TTL; when kv retention=10s we see better p95 in 15s bursts but not in 5s bursts (makes sense).

Deeper traces notes:
- Server spans show a distinct gap between "scheduling start" and "compute start" of ~80–450ms for many p99 events when cold. This gap disappears in prewarmed runs.
- GPU nvml shows small spikes in memory alloc/free right at burst boundary; correlate with the scheduling gap.
- No kernel OOMs or driver level errors in dmesg.
- Network RTT negligible (under 2ms) so networking not culprit here.

Hypothesis (what to test next):
1) Kernel/JIT warm-up is the dominant cold tail contributor. Test: force a compile-only warm step (like we did with prewarm) vs a minimal dummy inference and compare. If compile-only reduces tail similarly, JIT is main culprit.
2) KV cache decay is secondary and mostly impacts mid-tail; test by toggling kv retention aggressively and instrumenting per-shard kv-hit rate at token granularity.
3) Memory allocator latency for large device allocations might be part of the schedule->compute gap. Try preallocating per-model buffer pool before bursts.

Short to-dos / next runs:
- [ ] Run A/B where prewarm = compile-only vs prewarm = dummy small request. Track p99 delta. (assign to Arjun)
- [ ] Add an experiment where we preallocate model weights and KV with a background task 60s before burst to separate allocation vs JIT. (self)
- [ ] Re-run with a smaller model (1.3B) to see scale effect — if p99 drops significantly relative, some part is model-size dependent. (Maya)
- [ ] Try a small quantized variant to see if kernel paths diverge and affect cold tail differently.

Notes to self / mental model updates:
- Practical mitigation path for prod: cheap periodic prewarm (every ~60s) reduces cold p99 significantly with minimal cost; but we need cost model for continuously prewarming large fleets. Also look into lazy compile caching across containers so prewarm can be amortized.
- Need to log "scheduling start -> compute start" as a standard span so we can quantify in prod.

Quick links & references used while running tests:
- INF-2345 (Jira) for microburst incident notes
- PR 789 (serving-runtime) where I toggled kv prefetch flag

Misc / random thoughts:
- Could we implement a lightweight kernel-warm RPC during idle that only touches a tiny subset of kernels? If JIT is the big cost, targeting the hot-kernel subset should give most of the benefit.
- For Dedicated customers with hard SLOs, include an optional prewarm policy in rollout config.

End of log. Will update after the compile-only A/B and preallocation runs.
